text: Imagine… you look up, and there is a second Earth in the sky.
Blue oceans. White clouds. Hanging right where the Moon should be.
And nobody knows… where it came from.
It starts on an ordinary evening. Just after sunset, a planet rises over the mountains.
It is as far away as the Moon. But it looks almost four times as wide.
Night one. The sky never gets dark.
This Earth reflects more than thirty times as much light as a full Moon. Your shadow lies sharp on the snow.
Within an hour, half the planet is outside, looking up.
But here’s the first problem. It is eighty-one times heavier than the Moon.
Day two. Its pull drags the oceans. On the coasts, the tides would rise tens of metres. Twice a day.
Even the rock under your feet rises and falls, by many metres. You just can’t feel it.
Day nine. At dusk, the other Earth is only a thin crescent.
Its night side is facing you.
And across the darkness… tiny lights appear.
And here’s the twist. Somewhere up there, someone is standing by a lake… looking up. At you.
If you could send them one message… what would you say?
